sources.entry: Wavo - Dictation that doesn't slow your Mac down: it runs on the Neural Engine, keeps your voice off the cloud, and types what you say wherever you're typing. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/vladkens/wavo-app) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Wavo is a free, local dictation app for macOS, Windows and Linux that transcribes speech on-device (GPU or Apple Neural Engine) and types the text into whatever app has focus.
use_cases: dictate messages or documents instead of typing
voice input for chats, editors and terminals
offline speech-to-text on a laptop without cloud accounts
transcribing short recordings and re-running transcription
voice typing on Linux under Wayland or X11
how_to_run: Download the file for your system from the latest release and run it.
Pick a model in Settings › Models (Parakeet Ultra is the default, about 0.7 GB, downloaded once).
Hold Option-Space (Ctrl+Alt+Space on Windows and Linux), speak, and let go; a short tap starts a longer dictation that the next press ends.
notable: Runs on the Apple Neural Engine on macOS 15+, claimed 61 ms for 11 s of speech on an M2
Native UI per OS rather than a webview app
Uses the standard Hugging Face cache so other tools can share models
Automatic microphone choice and searchable history with recordings, playback and export
Can import a history export from Handy
caveats: Windows installer is not yet code-signed, so SmartScreen warns on first run
On Linux the hotkey needs a desktop with global shortcuts (KDE Plasma 6, GNOME 48+, Hyprland); elsewhere a manual desktop shortcut is required
GNOME needs the AppIndicator extension for the tray; without a Vulkan driver it runs on CPU, much slower
Initial model download of about 0.7 GB is required
